units.translation: Πέμπει σὺν δορὶ δίκας πράκτορι θούριος ὄρνις Τευκρίδ᾽ ἐπ᾽ αἰαν [The rushing bird sends with the spear the avenger of justice to the Teucrian land], where the gloss δίκας [of justice] explains two words of the poet, which Aristophanes preserved in Frogs 1288: πέμπει σύν δορὶ καὶ χερὶ πράκτορι [sends with spear and avenging hand], although this reading labors under a slight corruption. For since the verse is antispastic dactylic tetrameter catalectic in disyllabum and therefore ends with a spondee, πράκτορι [avenger] cannot have been placed by Aeschylus in the strophe, who had written πράκτωρ [avenger]: if the scribes had left it untouched after the datives σὺν δορὶ καὶ χερί [with spear and hand], it would be much more surprising than that they changed it to πράκτορι [avenger]. But rightly the eagle, by whose portentous authority the Atreidae had been sent against Troy to exact vengeance, is called πράκτωρ [avenger], who πέμπει σὺν δορὶ καὶ χερί [sends with spear and hand], i.e. with arms and men. This I said in the Preface to the Leipzig edition, fifth, p. LXXXII.
Πράκτορες αἵματος αὐτῷ [avengers of blood for him]
Δῖον ἐπιδόμενοι πράκτορά τε σκοπὸν [having given a divine avenger and watcher]
πράκτορα πάνσκοπον [all-seeing avenger] Hermann. Cf. s.v. σκοπός [watcher].
The rushing bird sends with the spear the avenger of justice to the Teucrian land
having given a divine avenger and watcher
Ταχεῖά γ᾽ ἦλθε χρησμών [swift indeed came the fulfillment of the oracles]
swift indeed came the fulfillment of the oracles
having obtained well from the mind
guiding the helm of the mind well
for dark and shadowy paths of the mind stretch out
to do, act; to exact punishment, avenge; to fare

πράσσειν [to fare] is used intransitively of the state of affairs in which one finds oneself (many examples of this kind are collected in Thes. vol. 6 p. 1570-1573), usually with an adverb, such as εὐ [well], κακῶς [badly], καλῶς [finely].
πράσσω [I do] with accusative: I suffer
